why: I65 (tests_m3/test_o12.py rule O8, at the I65 prereg) adds laws/M2/L_contract_C_o12.json, a law of subform intended_weak (an intent contract's L_weak, I64 K3), with a PROVED record, and lists it in laws/M2/REGISTRY.json (its statement and the view gen/M2/extracted/m1_view.json in facts_files), a sha256-pinned input of spec/M3/lib/lean_promoted.json. Such a law is outside I43's promoted set: its statement has a ghost term no Lean emitter renders (its lean4 entry is not_run unsupported_form, rule O4), so tests_m3/_i43.promoted_doc, which renders every PROVED law and raises on one it cannot, does not apply to it. The amended test checks the inputs and recomputes the document over a copy of the tree without the intended_weak laws, their records and their registry entries (the registry written as holon derive writes it, which reproduces the pinned bytes when nothing else changed); at the I65 prereg there is no such law and it reads the tree itself, as before.

I65 (tests_m3/test_o12.py rule O8, at the I65 prereg) adds one PROVED law of subform intended_weak to laws/M2 (an intent contract's L_weak, outside I43's promoted set: rule O4 gives it lean4 not_run unsupported_form). The live PROVED set the test compares with the sidecar's leaves such laws out; the sidecar counts and every other check are unchanged.

I43-R1 lets no record outside the sidecar's attempted laws gain a lean4 entry. I65 (tests_m3/test_o12.py rule O8, at the I65 prereg) adds the PROVED record of an intended_weak law (an intent contract's L_weak), outside the promoted set, and G7 requires exactly one lean4 entry on it (not_run, unsupported_form; rule O4). The amended test exempts the records of intended_weak laws from that one loop; the statuses, the Bend files and the unregenerated records are checked as before.

results/M2/metrics.json counts every PROVED record of results/M2 in cross_kernel_coverage, which after I65 (tests_m3/test_o12.py rule O8, at the I65 prereg) includes one law of subform intended_weak (an intent contract's L_weak, outside I43's promoted set). The amended test subtracts the PROVED records of intended_weak laws from the reported count before comparing it with the sidecar's; the required fields are checked as before.

I43-R3 holds each Lean directory to exactly the sidecar's model files, report.json and the files of its attempted laws. I65 (tests_m3/test_o12.py rule O8, at the I65 prereg; rule O4) adds to results/M2 the PROVED record of an intended_weak law (an intent contract's L_weak over the window view gen/M2/extracted/m1_view.json), outside I43's promoted set: it has no Lean law file (lean4 not_run unsupported_form), but I43's own rule L4 gives its directory a model file for every Bend model its laws use, so gen/M2/lean gains models/m1_view.lean, which the frozen sidecar does not list. The amended test lets a directory also hold the model file of each of its intended_weak laws' Bend models (intended_weak_models: models/<stem of the record's model>.lean), and nothing else; --check and every other file are checked as before.

I43-R9 holds every .lean file of the Lean directories to be a sidecar law's file or a sidecar model, obeying its file rules. I65 (tests_m3/test_o12.py rule O8, at the I65 prereg; rule O4) adds, under I43's rule L4, the model file of an intended_weak law's Bend model to gen/M2/lean (models/m1_view.lean), which the frozen sidecar does not list. The amended test checks such a file with tests_m3/_i43.file_check's model rules, without the sidecar's interface, which it has none of; any other file is checked as before.

I26: I26's prereg (0f11f2b; key I26) adds five FACT laws to results/M3 over spec/M2/facts/morph_rollup.extracted.json, the holon-facts/0.3 document no Lean emitter reads, and its P4 predicts one of them PROVED. rendered() carved out exactly the rule-DISCH laws (the human's answer at the move onto be95d6d: laws whose facts no emitter reads are not attempted, PROVED or REFUTED, as I30's typed and I27's UNDO laws; holon.lean._attempted states the same rule by kind) and raised Unsupported for any other PROVED law of kind other, so once a PROVED FACT law existed no tree could satisfy both keys (every test that renders the scope errored). The amended rendered() carves out rule FACT the same way, with its own reason FACT_NOT_ATTEMPTED (a new constant); every other PROVED law outside the emitters' kinds still raises, and nothing else in the instrument changes.

I26: the same conflict (the FACT carve-out above). The scope check compares every PROVED record with the prereg's sidecar laws; I26's PROVED FACT law, merged after the prereg and carved out as I31's DISCH laws are, is not in that sidecar. The amended check leaves the records of rule FACT out of that one comparison; the counts, the attempted sets, the DISCH carve-out and every other assertion are unchanged.

I66 (tests_m3/test_view_evidence.py rule V8, at the I66 prereg; Question Q62, the route I65's prereg names for a window view's evidence) models holon.differential's window view gen/M2/extracted/m1_view.json in M2's evidence set, so gen/M2/evidence.json's evidence_sha256 changes and holon derive copies the new value into laws/M2/REGISTRY.json (I15: the registry's evidence_sha256 is the set's), a sha256-pinned input of spec/M3/lib/lean_promoted.json; I43's promoted set reads only the registry's statements. The amended test compares that one input through pinned_sha256: when the registry's evidence_sha256 is the one the committed gen/M2/evidence.json of the tree under test holds, that value is the set's own body hash (the set without evidence_sha256 and inputs, as canonical JSON: I14) and it is not the value the I66 key records (thresholds.registry_at_prereg), the registry's text as holon derive writes it, with the recorded value set back, must hash to the pin; any other change of the registry, or a set whose evidence_sha256 is not its own hash, still fails. So the test accepts the registry following any later rebuild of the committed set, not only I66's, which no claim of I43 depends on. Every other input, the record baselines and the recomputation are checked as before. At the I66 prereg the registry is its pinned self, so the test checks what it checked before. It already fails at the base e215fbf5, as at fde1f819, on 103 laws/M3 inputs moved by I26's catalog bump (I26's Question 5) and on two typed M3 records' baselines; this amendment neither causes nor hides that.
